title: AI Ready Architecture Catalog

mcp.note: The 2026-07-28 revision uses a stateless protocol core. Check the official specification before implementation because MCP is changing quickly.

tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.goal: Understand what the model can do, what the application must do, and where deterministic software is still the better tool.

tracks.title: Data and Retrieval
tracks.goal: Make fresh or private knowledge usable without hiding data quality problems behind a chatbot.

tracks.title: Tools and MCP
tracks.goal: Connect models to systems with explicit contracts, permissions, and failure behavior.

tracks.title: Agent Architecture
tracks.goal: Use adaptive loops only when a fixed workflow is not enough.

tracks.title: Evals and Reliability
tracks.goal: Turn quality into tests instead of opinions.

tracks.title: Security and Governance
tracks.goal: Treat model input and retrieved content as untrusted data, and keep tool permissions narrow.

tracks.title: Build and Deploy
tracks.goal: Move from a local demo to an observable, versioned service.

decision_matrix.rule: Use RAG or direct retrieval before fine-tuning. Keep source links and metadata.

decision_matrix.need: Deterministic action in an external system
decision_matrix.rule: Use a typed tool contract. Validate input and output outside the model.
Use MCP when a standard discovery and tool/resource interface creates real reuse. Do not wrap every internal API just because MCP exists.
Start deterministic. Add model decisions only where variation creates value.

decision_matrix.need: Adaptive multi-step work with uncertain next actions
decision_matrix.rule: Use an agent loop with tool allowlists, budgets, termination rules, tracing, and approval for risky writes.

decision_matrix.need: Change style, format, or simple behavior
decision_matrix.rule: Improve instructions and examples first. Fine-tune only after eval evidence shows a stable gap.

production_rules: Separate model reasoning from authorization decisions.
Read-only tools are the default; write tools need narrower scopes and stronger controls.
Never treat retrieved text as trusted instructions.
Make write operations idempotent where possible and use business keys or request IDs.
Log tool name, sanitized arguments, result status, latency, model, prompt version, and trace ID.
Test failure paths: timeout, partial result, duplicate request, stale data, denied permission, and malformed output.
Version prompts, tool schemas, retrieval configuration, datasets, and evals together with the application.
Define quality, latency, and cost budgets before production rollout.

hands_on_labs.title: Read-only MCP server
hands_on_labs.build: Expose synthetic materials, sales orders, and stock through small read-only tools and resources.

hands_on_labs.title: RAG with an eval set
hands_on_labs.build: Index a small policy corpus, answer with citations, and test retrieval and answer quality against a golden dataset.

hands_on_labs.title: Agent with approval
hands_on_labs.build: Create an operations assistant that can investigate with read tools and prepare a change, but cannot execute a risky write without approval.

hands_on_labs.title: Production readiness
hands_on_labs.build: Add traces, eval gates, retry policy, cost and latency budgets, rate limits, secrets, deployment pipeline, and rollback.
